subject: Renewal billing consolidation to Azure Marketplace
messages:
From: Mark Ellis <mark.ellis@stellardx.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@stellardx.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal coming up — can we move to Azure billing?

Hi Aditya,

Hope you’re well. Our renewal for Redwood services is coming up on 2026-12-15. Procurement is asking whether we can shift billing to the Azure Marketplace subscription instead of paying Redwood directly — this would help us consolidate ERP flows and use our committed Azure credits.

Asha (cc) is leading procurement — can you outline what the migration path looks like and whether our committed SKUs and volume discounts will carry over? We’re also evaluating whether a marketplace invoice can reflect the same start/end dates and discounts.

High level asks:
- Is Redwood set up as an Azure Marketplace SaaS offer for direct billing?
- What paperwork or change-of-billing steps do you need from our side?
- Any gotchas that could affect our renewal or the committed spend?

Thanks — we’d like to decide by the end of November.

—Mark
Director of Cloud Procurement
StellarDX

From: aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
To: Mark Ellis <mark.ellis@stellardx.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, priyom_das@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — can we move to Azure billing?

Mark — thanks for the note and heads up. Short answer: yes, we can transition the renewal to Azure Marketplace billing, but there are a few administrative and timing items we should coordinate so you don’t lose discounts or committed pricing. I’ve looped in Ben (AE) for commercial details and Priyom (marketplace ops) for the technical/offer-side steps.

Quick summary of what I’ll do:
- Ben will propose a short MAP (mutual action plan) with dates and owner tasks.
- Priyom will confirm which entitlement mapping we’ll use so your committed SKUs map cleanly to the marketplace offer.
- I’ll coordinate DocuSign and any procurement artifacts we need to send to you.

I’ve attached a short MA summary to describe the items we typically move during a billing consolidation.

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben to send MAP and timeline (target by Fri 11/13)
2) Quick 30-min call next week to confirm PO and DocuSign flow
3) Priyom to validate offer mapping and confirm whether billing dates can be preserved

When’s good for a call? I have availability Wed 11/11 afternoon.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: StellarDX_MA_Summary.pdf (summary of typical billing consolidation items)

From: ben_carter@redwood.example.com
To: Mark Ellis <mark.ellis@stellardx.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.example.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — can we move to Azure billing? — Proposed MAP

Mark / Aditya — thanks. Per Aditya, here’s a concise Mutual Action Plan to get StellarDX from direct billing -> Azure Marketplace subscription before your 12/15 renewal. I kept the timeline tight but achievable.

Mutual Action Plan (high level):
1) 11/13 — Align on commercial terms (discounts, term length, start date). Owner: Ben (Redwood) / Mark (StellarDX)
2) 11/15 — Provide PO or committed order form to Redwood (if required). Owner: StellarDX procurement
3) 11/18 — Redwood to generate marketplace offer and send DocuSign link for acceptance. Owner: Redwood (Ben + Aditya)
4) 11/20 — Marketplace onboarding (technical entitlements & listing) completed. Owner: Priyom (Redwood ops)
5) 12/01 — Final invoice cut and subscription activation in Azure portal. Owner: Redwood billing + StellarDX procurement

Notes / commercial clarifications:
- We can preserve your negotiated volume discounts if the purchase is executed as a conversion to an equivalent SKU subscription in the Azure offer. That requires the PO to reference the same committed quantities and the same start date.
- If StellarDX needs an exact invoice date alignment to match revenue recognition windows, let us know and we’ll flag with billing.

Action items for Mark: please confirm whether StellarDX can sign the DocuSign by 11/22 and whether procurement can issue a PO referencing the negotiated SKUs.

DocuSign link will be provided by 11/18. I’ll attach a PO template to help speed procurement.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps.

—Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: StellarDX_PO-template.docx

From: priyom_das@redwood.example.com
To: Mark Ellis <mark.ellis@stellardx.com>, ben_carter@redwood.example.com, aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — can we move to Azure billing? — Marketplace steps & checklist

Hi all — I kicked off the marketplace prep and attached the Azure checklist. A few technical items I want to call out so we don’t hit delays:

1) Offer mapping: we’ll map your current committed SKU "redwood-standard-500k" to the Azure offer meter of the same name. That preserves pricing tiers.
2) Contract/PO: The PO should reference the Marketplace offer ID or the Redwood order form number we’ll include in the DocuSign packet. This avoids manual reconciliation downstream.
3) Billing date alignment: Azure Marketplace subscriptions typically activate when the marketplace transaction completes; we can request an effective start date to match 12/15 but it requires a back-dated effective date in the DocuSign which Azure accepts in limited cases. I’ll flag this in our onboarding ticket.
4) Transfer of committed credits: Marketplace billing does not automatically migrate third-party enterprise agreements or committed credits — that’s on the customer side. If StellarDX expects committed Azure credits to pay the invoice, confirm with your Microsoft AM.

I’ve attached the checklist and the initial listing metadata we plan to submit this week. If everything looks good I’ll create the onboarding ticket in the Marketplace portal and share the DocuSign link once the listing is ready.

Attachment: azure-marketplace-checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Marketplace Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Mark Ellis <mark.ellis@stellardx.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, aditya_rao@redwood.example.com, priyom_das@redwood.example.com
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@stellardx.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — can we move to Azure billing? — RE: Agreement and PO timeline

Thanks everyone — appreciate the clear plan. Asha confirms procurement can issue a PO referencing the SKUs and the Redwood order form number; we’ll aim to sign DocuSign by 11/22 but given internal approvals our practical target is 11/24.

Two clarifying questions before we lock dates:
1) If the marketplace subscription goes live on 12/01 (per the MAP), can we still have the invoice reflect a 12/15 service start to match our fiscal calendar? We’ll need that for revenue deferral on our side.
2) Who should I put in the Microsoft AM thread so they can confirm the use of committed credits against the marketplace invoice? Asha will reach out to the AM but wants a Redwood contact listed.

If both are OK we’ll proceed with the PO and expect the DocuSign by 11/24.

—Mark
Director of Cloud Procurement
StellarDX
